featured_reviews.name: rohan vaswani
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Experience with Piramal Group – Repeated Defaults on Written Commitments

I am sharing this purely as my personal experience and opinion, based on direct interactions with Piramal Group’s senior representatives.

I was given multiple explicit assurances, including a specific written commitment that a credit note would be issued by 8 February. That promise has now been missed, repeatedly, without explanation, ownership, or even basic communication—despite escalations to senior management.

When an organisation of this scale fails to honour simple, routine financial commitments after multiple follow-ups, it raises serious concerns about internal accountability, governance, and execution discipline. What is most worrying is not the delay itself, but the complete absence of transparency or ownership.

As a customer, this experience has significantly eroded my confidence. Repeated missed timelines and silence create the unfortunate perception that commitments are made casually and honoured selectively.

I would strongly advise prospective customers to document everything in writing, be cautious with assurances, and factor in delays—even when commitments are made at senior levels.

This review reflects my experience alone, but it has been deeply disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Rajkunwar Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointed with the After-Sales Experience

I would strongly advise against booking a property here. The after-sales service has been extremely poor, and the customer relationship management is frustrating to deal with. The CRM team seems to be trained only to follow up for payments and installations — any genuine customer concerns are consistently ignored.

We received an official invite claiming the amenities were completed and ready for viewing. We travelled from another city just for this, only to find that barely 10% of the amenities were ready — just two indoor rooms (Pilates & Cycling). This was highly misleading.

Despite making multiple visits — including two personal trips I made flying in from London — we have still not been shown the floor view of the completed building (South), even though that is a basic request. Our unit is in a different tower, but our only request was to see the floor view of a completed tower. Every time, we’ve been met with excuses like “we don’t have the keys” — even though possession hasn’t started yet.

The customer service is apathetic at best. Calls go unanswered, and emails regarding even simple customer requirements are ignored.

If this is the service before possession, it raises serious concerns about what can be expected after moving in.

featured_reviews.name: Anand Parikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
DO NOT BOOK. Read this:
1. SRA: Humungous SRA kissing back of north and central towers. For upto 20 floors,  you'll litrally wake up next to SRA residents, if you are in units facing behind. This giant SRA is just the start. These guys have over 10 acres behind PM, which can lead to more SRAs in future.
2. Access road: 2 access roads. Babu Sakpal road is filthy beyond imagination. I gagged multiple times when I was surveying neighborhood. Never smelled anything so bad. This is also entry to SRA. Police petroling very frequent here. Other access is through Arthur road, 2 blocks from Arthur Rd. jail. So you can expect some disturbance on that.
3. Builder quotes: Please read each line on cost sheet very carefully. They've quoted different price everytime I visited. They'll push you for really unacceptable units in north tower. Review GST charges carefully. They know exactly where all they've messed up. So they'll only show higher floor in south tower to you.
4. Possible criminal activities in area: The SRA behind has 50+ units per floor and 40+ floors. These SRA units are already selling in black market. You can imagine what kind of people will buy these 400 sq. ft. units for a cr. Let me give you a hint, they're not going to be slum dweller. Still not clear? Read Saat rasta history.
Builder finish is good, but does not compensate for negatives. Worth waiting for OC so you can at least see what you're paying for in this strangely marketed/ located property. Mahalaxmi is good real estate micromarket, but avoid this property for sure.

Think Twice Before Booking
Please be careful before booking a unit here. We’ve had a frustrating experience post-booking. There’s barely any support from the CRM team — calls and emails are rarely answered unless it’s about payments.

We were invited to view completed amenities — and arrived with high expectations. Only to be shown two indoor rooms. No communication, no accountability.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket Khaire
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had a terrible experience staying at this Flat 118, Shreepati Wing C and would advise anyone considering booking it to look elsewhere. My stay was plagued by a number of issues that made the accommodation completely unsuitable for anyone.

Firstly, there were reports of paranormal activity within the flat. It was believed that a policeman's soul was haunting the property, which made my stay extremely unsettling and uncomfortable. I felt constantly on edge and never truly felt safe during my time there.

In addition to this, the room lacked natural sunlight, which made it feel very claustrophobic and depressing. The limited amount of daylight that did filter in only highlighted the dinginess of the space.

Furthermore, the water supply was limited to just one hour per day, which made it extremely difficult to shower or carry out any basic hygiene practices. This was unacceptable and made my stay very unpleasant.

The owner of the flat (Mohan Thevar) was also terrible. He was rude, unresponsive and unhelpful when we raised concerns about the property. It was clear that he didn't care about our experience and was only interested in taking our money.When one small girl died, due to builder negligence and my sister saw it. We immediately told him and he was saying "ye toh hote rehta hai". He didn't even returned our security deposit on time. He took 5k from it. The worst human alive on this planet, who only cares about money.

There is no mobile network coming in this flat.
Alot of time we missed important calls.

To top it all off, the building was infested with cockroaches and rats. The presence of these pests was disgusting and made the flat feel very unsanitary. I was constantly on edge and felt like I couldn't relax or enjoy my time there.

Overall, I would strongly advise anyone to avoid this flat at all costs. It was a terrible experience that I would never want to repeat.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nestled amidst the lush landscapes of Srisailam Highway, Primal Aranya is less of a residential development and more of an ecological statement. It represents a sophisticated departure from the sterile, concrete-heavy luxury often found in modern urban sprawl, pivoting instead toward a "forest-first" philosophy that seamlessly integrates high-end living with the raw tranquility of nature.
The architectural intent here is clearly biophilic, emphasizing expansive open spaces, natural ventilation, and a layout that honors the existing topography. What distinguishes Aranya is its commitment to "Quiet Luxury"—it avoids the ostentatious in favor of organic textures, curated greenery, and an infrastructure that promotes wellness. The amenities are thoughtfully decentralized, ensuring that whether you are at the clubhouse or on a jogging trail, the boundary between the built environment and the wilderness remains beautifully blurred.
From an investment perspective, its strategic location near the Pharma City and the ORR ensures robust appreciation, yet the project feels worlds away from the industrial hum. It caters perfectly to the discerning homeowner who seeks a sanctuary that doesn’t compromise on connectivity. Primal Aranya isn't just offering a plot or a villa; it is offering a rhythmic way of life governed by the seasons rather than the clock. For those looking to escape the hyper-compressed lifestyle of central Hyderabad without sacrificing modern comforts, Aranya stands as a premier benchmark in sustainable luxury.

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Malkoti
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are certain pro and cons about the society and It is better to point them out one by one.

Pro:
1) The location is very near to the Byculla railway station, 5 min walking distance.
2) 1BHK Flat size is OK for a couple (no more than that).
3) Rent is relatively less as compared to nearby societies.
4) No problem for parking a two-wheeler.

Cons:
1) Though it is a registered society but the most basic facilities are not available.

2) Water supply is limited (few hours only), especially in winters.  For some wicked logic, they don't allow storage tanks in some wings.

3) Common floor area is not cleaned as sweepers don't show up (almost ever) and eventually it is you who has to do the cleaning job. The stairs are stains with spitted-tobacco red marks.

4) There is no door-step garbage collection facility you have to carry it outside yourself. For this reason, some people just throw the garbage outside their window resulting in filthy ground floor.

5) The mobile signal reception is very poor for inside flats. You will be having a hard time using the internet.

6) The center of the building behaves like a duct and thus makes even a small sound feel like loud noise.

7) You won't find any big shopping complex like Reliance fresh/D-Mart nearby What they offer is a delivery point.

8) The parks/grounds nearby are very small for morning/evening walks. The best you would find is Race-course but that's main entrance is nearly 3.5 km away.

9) The place security doesn't have a telephone system to inform about visitors. Security guys basically allow everyone.

10) The information disbursal system in the society is very bad, sometimes they use loudspeakers which is kind of annoying!

11) First few floor rooms are almost devoid of sunlight.
